title: The Epidemiological Characteristics and Spatiotemporal Clustering of Measles - China, 2005-2022.
ehr_evidence: We obtained measles reporting data from the China Disease Prevention and Control Information System to assess the epidemiological characteristics of measles based on the date of illness onset.
summary: A spatiotemporal surveillance analysis of measles epidemiology in China from 2005 to 2022 using national infectious disease reporting data, examining incidence trends and spatial clustering.
key_findings: A total of 732,218 measles cases were reported in China from 2005 to 2022, with a male-to-female ratio of 1.43:1 and an average reported incidence of 3.00 per 100,000.
The average annual percentage change (AAPC) was -31.55 (95% CI: -43.03, -27.12, P<0.05), indicating a significant decline in incidence from 2005 to 2022.
The highest incidence was observed in the 0-4 year age group at 26.03 per 100,000, and infants had the highest incidence at 75.41 per 100,000, with 51.18% of cases in children under 5 years old.
Significant global spatial clustering of measles was identified during 2010-2011 and 2014-2017 (Moran's I values over 0, P<0.05), with no global spatial clustering observed after 2017.
The high-risk spatiotemporal cluster persisted from 2005 to 2008 (RR=4.69, LLR=140,816, P<0.001), while the low-risk cluster persisted from 2016 to 2022 (RR=0.08, LLR=113,675, P<0.001).
population: All reported measles cases in China (excluding Hong Kong SAR, Macao SAR, and Taiwan), 2005-2022, predominantly young children
exposure_domain: none (spatiotemporal surveillance, no environmental exposure assessed)
limitations: Using provincial administrative divisions as spatial units might underestimate clustering and fail to identify some localized outbreaks or epidemics.
Some data from the years immediately following the 2004 implementation of the reporting system may have information biases such as underreporting or misreporting.
